title: Vela glitch phases show no excess order in a 300 to 3000 day search under shuffled waiting times
abstract: We search 300 to 3000 day periods in 21 large Vela pulsar glitches. The largest squared mean phase vector is 0.1920 near 1164 days. Shuffled waiting times give a full-search upper-tail fraction of 0.9856. A period and phase fitted to 14 early events give a mean cosine of 0.1689 for seven later events, with a tail fraction of 0.2836. Blocked shuffles, two event cuts, a finer grid and epoch changes give no phase excess. Four separately published epochs barely change the scores. The test is conditional on observed waits and assumes exchangeable intervals. It cannot exclude all clocks; equal waits make the shuffle test powerless. No new source is found. Code, aggregate results, a figure, hashes and external retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Period search and interval-shuffle controls for 21 Vela steps of at least 1e-7. Black lines show measured scores. Each control repeats the full fit. The null conditions on the observed waiting times.

citations.reason: Earlier Vela size-to-wait test identifies the frozen shared catalog and the effect of event cuts. This study tests phase order and reuses no code.
Known size and waiting-time structure motivates a null that preserves intervals.
Four separately fitted recent epochs provide a limited measurement check.
Recent joint waiting-time and size analysis; not a phase-clock test.
